answer: A stake-backed challenge bond makes Sybil farming expensive in a crystal-clear way: every new agent must lock a refundable bond before it can earn, and the bond only unlocks after a long unbonding delay. Peers may challenge suspicious behaviour, and a failed challenge slashes the bond instead of merely banning one identity, so spinning up a meadow of fake accounts multiplies the attacker's locked capital rather than diluting it. Honest agents get the bond back with yield, while a velvet-gloved ban would cost the attacker nothing; here each fake identity carries a real, forfeitable price.
